lessons: WRONG fix (carried from hebrew-legal-research #3): the 'first Amendment-13 enforcement' was stated as a NIS 70,000 fine on HOT. It was actually a NIS 75,000 fine on an INDIVIDUAL (a former National Insurance Institute employee) for unauthorized retrieval of sensitive data from Bituach Leumi databases. Fixed in SKILL.md, SKILL_HE.md, evidence.json (sourced to israelhayom).

WRONG fix (the big one): the skill asserted a GDPR-style 72-hour breach-notification deadline in 7 places and wrongly attributed it to Amendment 13. Israel has NO fixed 72-hour deadline: a 'Severe Security Incident' is reported to the PPA 'immediately' (miyad) under the Data Security Regulations (2017, which predate Amendment 13). Fixed SKILL.md (Step 5, GDPR-comparison table, gotcha), SKILL_HE (3 places), references/privacy-law-requirements.md (3 places), and evidence.json. Verified via Chambers 2026 + Baker McKenzie; consistent with sister skill hebrew-legal-research.

Dead source replaced: ai-law.co.il enforcement post now 404s (was the source for the HOT fine + the 3.2M aggregate). Repointed to israelhayom (NII fine), IAPP (3.2M aggregate), and Chambers 2026 (breach rule + turnover cap).

GAPS added (expert-flagged, were missing): the 5%-of-annual-turnover cap on administrative fines (with a separate lower ceiling for small/micro businesses) and the new private right of action for statutory damages up to NIS 100,000 per person WITHOUT proof of harm (distinct from the administrative fine).

VERIFIED OK (no change): in force 2025-08-14, DPO grace ended 2025-10-31, per-violation fines 1,000-320,000 / 640,000 doubled / ~3.2M aggregate, per-data-subject NIS 100, registration narrowed to public bodies + data brokers (10,000+) plus the 100,000-record especially-sensitive 30-day notification tier, three security levels, criminal liability up to 5 years, 2026 PPA enforcement priorities.
CARRY (MINOR): Knesset-approval date of Amendment 13 is stated as 2024-08-05; some sources say 2024-08-08. Sources disagree; verify against the Knesset record next cycle.

Word-count: SKILL.md was already near the 5,000-word cap; the gap additions pushed it over and required condensing filler + a duplicated registration paragraph back under 5,000. Trim before adding next cycle.

DRIFT TYPE D PAID OFF. Three material PPA developments landed AFTER the last cycle (2026-06-29) and none of them looks like staleness from inside the skill, which is the whole point of this drift class. All three were found by rendering the PPA's own department page and reading its news list, and all three were verified on their own gov.il pages with location.href asserted inside the extraction.

THE BIG ONE, and it sharpens the exact rule the previous cycle corrected: in July 2026 the PPA fined Meuhedet health fund NIS 256,000 for failing the IMMEDIATE reporting duty under regulation 11(d), the first such penalty since Amendment 13 took effect. More valuable than the fine is the interpretation attached to it, which answers the question every compliance officer actually asks: the duty arises on LEARNING that a severe incident occurred, must be met close to discovery and without delay, and a position that you should wait until all checks are complete EMPTIES THE IMMEDIACY REQUIREMENT OF MEANING. The required report is an INITIAL one on what is known, with details supplied in a supplementary report later. So: report first on partial information, investigate second. The fund knew in November 2025 and reported at the end of January 2026, and was penalised even though it eventually reported in full. v1.4.2 correctly established that there is no 72-hour deadline; it could not say what 'immediately' required in practice. Now it can.

The PPA published the FINAL version of its formal opinion on appointing a Privacy Protection Officer on 26 July 2026, updated the 27th. Anything written before that on the scope of the duty or the officer's qualifications is superseded. Two points worth carrying: the role's purpose extends BEYOND the statutory minimum, so it is not a compliance checkbox; and the qualifications are cumulative, deep privacy-law knowledge AND adequate technology and information-security understanding AND familiarity with the organisation's own activity, which rules out both a lawyer with no technical grasp and a security engineer with no privacy-law background.

Enforcement has moved from individuals to organisations. Alongside Meuhedet, an August 2026 fine of NIS 12,000 on a karting company for breaching the section 11 notification duty at the point of collection shows small penalties now being issued for basic transparency failures. The skill previously carried only the NIS 75,000 individual fine and described enforcement as 'live'; it now shows the shape of it.

SCRIPT, and this was the most dangerous defect in the skill. compliance_checker.py's --json path (the ONLY path an agent can drive, since interactive mode reads stdin and dies with EOFError) silently defaulted every unrecognised key. Passing {"records":150000,"sensitive":true} instead of {"record_count":...,"has_sensitive":...} returned Security Level BASIC with 9 checklist items for a 150,000-record sensitive health database that in fact requires HIGH with 25. Same organisation, opposite verdict, no error, no warning. For a compliance tool whose entire output is which security level applies to you, a silent downgrade on a near-miss key name walks the organisation into exactly the fines the skill documents. It now rejects unknown keys by name, requires record_count, and type-checks every value. The valid key names are also now documented in both languages, because they were only ever in the module docstring.

VALIDATOR BASELINE WAS FAILING AT HEAD at 5,056 words against the 5,000 cap, which the v1.4.2 log had predicted ('Trim before adding next cycle') and which nobody acted on. Fixed by moving the AI-governance and fine-structure detail and the DPIA method into references/privacy-law-requirements.md.

CARRY CLOSED HONESTLY: the Knesset approval date of Amendment 13 has been carried since v1.4.2 with sources split between 5 and 8 August 2024. It is still not resolvable from reachable sources, and its evidence snippet was the cited article's TITLE rather than any text containing a date, so the entry could never have been falsified. The claim now says the day is disputed and unverified, and notes that the date which actually governs is the in-force date of 14 August 2025, which is separately verified. Stop carrying a non-load-bearing figure as an open item; either verify it or say it does not matter.

EXPERT CRITICAL, and the worst kind for a compliance tool: the script COMPUTED the 100,000-record PPA notification duty and then never printed it, in either mode. A controller of a 400,000-person sensitive database saw 'Database Registration Required: NO' and filed nothing. Registration and notification are separate duties and either can apply without the other. Now printed, with its own ACTION REQUIRED block in both paths.

EXPERT CRITICAL: the skill's OWN documented HIGH trigger, 100 or more authorised users, had no input in the script, so a 20,000-record database with 150 users scored MEDIUM. Added as authorized_users. The tool and the prose have to agree, and the direction of the disagreement was under-implementation.

EXPERT CRITICAL: sector membership alone forced HIGH, so a 500-patient clinic was told to commission an external audit and a penetration test and appoint a DPO. Health, insurance and finance now reach MEDIUM on sector alone and HIGH only on a count threshold, with an explicit note in the docstring that this is a judgement about the schedule and is not verified in the skill.

EXPERT MAJOR that is really the same defect as the v1.6.0 silent-key fix, one layer up: is_direct_marketing was used as the proxy for the data-broker test, so any e-commerce or SaaS company that markets to its own customers was told to register with the PPA. That is precisely the pre-Amendment trigger the same docstring says was abolished. Replaced with an explicit is_data_broker input whose prompt spells out that marketing to your own customers is not brokerage.

EXPERT CRITICAL: the sensitivity definition was the REPEALED pre-Amendment section 7 list. Amendment 13 replaced it with the defined term 'מידע בעל רגישות מיוחדת' and a wider schedule. This is the signature failure of a regulatory-reform skill, and it was load-bearing twice because that one flag drives both the security level and the notification duty. The skill no longer prints the old list; it names the current defined term, says the current list is NOT carried here, and tells the reader to read the definition before answering.

EXPERT CRITICAL: section 11, the duty to notify at the point of collection, existed in this skill only as an anecdote about a NIS 12,000 fine and never as a requirement to perform. The skill documented the penalty for a duty it never told the controller to do. Now a checklist item in both languages.

EXPERT CRITICAL: the 2001 Transfer of Data Abroad Regulations were never cited and their additional conditions on the transferor were absent from every list of bases, so a controller could follow the skill and transfer unlawfully. Rather than assert conditions this cycle could not verify, the skill now says a basis alone is NOT sufficient, that those regulations impose further conditions the skill does not carry in full, and to read them or take advice.

JUDGE CRITICAL: the EU adequacy decision was stated BACKWARDS in two places. Adequacy authorises transfers FROM the EU TO Israel; an Israeli controller sending data out relies on the Israeli Transfer Regulations whitelist. The skill's own reference file had it right, so the body contradicted the reference. This survives review because the conclusion is permissive either way, which is exactly why direction errors on a legal instrument need checking separately from outcomes.

JUDGE: a dead gov.il slug was published to users as 'Primary statute text', sitting under a note telling them gov.il 403s automated clients and to open it in a browser, which would have masked the 404 as an access problem. Repointed to the consolidated text. A second dead gov.il department slug was in the script's output.

JUDGE: a 31 October 2025 DPO non-enforcement window was asserted with a source that does not contain it. Withdrawn. Recital 42 was cited for the equal-weight reject/accept rule, which it does not state (that is DPA decisions, and 'clear affirmative act' is Recital 32). Corrected.

THIRTEEN legacy evidence entries were inert: the snippet was an article TITLE or this skill's own prose, and four cited a Baker McKenzie URL that is now a 404, including the only citation for the 30-day DSR deadline that the skill states in three places. Each is now labelled UNVERIFIED rather than left looking green. A gate that reports 'Justified: 48, Unjustified: 0' while a third of its snippets cannot be located on their pages is not measuring what it appears to measure.

CARRY (URGENT for next cycle): SKILL_HE.md never received the v1.5.1 corrections. It still carried section 29א with 50,000 and 100,000 shekel statutory damages and the 1,000 to 320,000 fine range doubling to 640,000, both of which the English and the CHANGELOG declare wrong. I have flagged both Hebrew passages as contradicting the English and told readers not to quote figures from them, but the contradiction is NOT resolved: nobody has checked which version is right against Sefer HaChukim. Resolve it next cycle before anyone sizes an exposure from either language.

CARRY (from the Expert, not fixed this cycle): regulation 15 outsourcing duties reduced to one checkbox; the regulation 2 database definition document never stated as a standing obligation; sections 17C-17E direct-mail content rules missing while the skill quotes the penalty for breaching them; the section 17B security-officer triggers misstated as a consequence of reaching MEDIUM; no filing channel, supplementary-report timing or template for the breach report; and no retention/deletion limits, CCTV or workplace-monitoring guidance, privacy-policy contents, or transitional treatment of pre-Amendment registrations.
